extracted.intended_audience: general encyclopedia readers and researchers interested in Reddit (users, moderators, PR/brand professionals researching Reddit practices)
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize evaluative standards, policies, and practical guidance about how Reddit communities are run, moderated, and engaged with (including content policy, moderator authority, AMA hosting, and brand engagement). Useful for people producing or evaluating behavior on Reddit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subreddit autonomy and moderator authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Each subreddit community is entitled to its own views, and moderators set and enforce community-specific rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reddit representatives have emphasized that statements or bans by subreddit moderators 'do not reflect the views of Reddit as a whole'; anyone can start their own subreddit devoted to particular views, opinions or interests. If you disagree with how a moderator manages a subreddit, the recommended practical solution is to create and moderate a new subreddit with different rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reddit content policy — prohibited content types
rubrics_metrics.description: Reddit's content policy and Help pages identify categories of prohibited content, including (explicitly referenced) 'suggestive or sexual content' of minors and 'promoting hate based on identity or vulnerability.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article cites multiple instances where Reddit took enforcement actions (banning subreddits, quarantining communities) based on content-policy violations such as hate speech, sexual content involving minors, doxxing and other harmful behavior. The policy is periodically updated and enforcement can include bans, quarantines, or removal of communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content moderation enforcement (bans, quarantines, removals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reddit enforces its policies via quarantining and banning entire subreddits or removing moderators/users when communities violate site rules or are judged to promote hate or other prohibited content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical examples include bans of major extremist or hate communities (alt-right, several pro-Trump forums), quarantines of infamous communities, and removal of moderators in protest situations. Enforcement decisions can provoke community backlash (blackouts, protests) and are part of how Reddit operationalizes its content policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMA hosting & verification best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful Ask Me Anything (AMA) sessions rely on organizers who verify that guests are who they say they are and coordinate logistics (role exemplified by staff like Victoria Taylor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page documents that Victoria Taylor 'helped organise guests for AMAs and worked to verify that people due to answer questions were who they said they were.' Removing or disrupting such staff can cause large-scale moderator protests and interruptions to AMA functionality. Guidance implied: verify identities, have dedicated coordinators, and maintain communication with volunteer moderators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brand engagement norms on Reddit (authenticity and listening)
rubrics_metrics.description: Brands and PR professionals should approach Reddit by listening first, prioritizing topic-based participation over overt commercialism, and aiming to build credibility rather than simply trying to make content go viral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple cited pieces advise: 'To Learn About reddit, Listen First'; 'posting to reddit is to build credibility'; 'The communities on Reddit don't want to feel used or exploited. That's where listening comes in.' Advertisers are warned to be honest and prepared to engage 'honestly — and cleverly' to win trust. If a branded interaction looks inauthentic, Reddit and its communities expect transparency and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical community-response strategy (if disagreeing with moderation)
rubrics_metrics.description: If users dislike how a subreddit is being moderated, the practical recommended response (from quoted communications staff) is to start a new subreddit and moderate it with different rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as the constructive alternative to public confrontation: build an alternate community organized around the desired rules and norms rather than attempting to overturn existing moderators' decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectations around transparency when platform staff act
rubrics_metrics.description: Reddit leadership and communications are expected to be transparent and accountable when controversies arise; failures or perceived secrecy can trigger user protests and petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article recounts episodes (executive dismissals, editing comments by staff, hiring controversies) where lack of clear communication by Reddit staff led to large-scale user backlash. Implied standard: platform actors should communicate clearly and openly about decisions affecting communities to avoid unrest.
